I have identified and resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrect when following prefetches back to the parent object.

### Cause
In `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset` (in [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py)), Django was unconditionally setting the parent `instance` into the reverse relation cache of each prefetched related object (`rel_obj`).

When the parent `instance` had deferred fields (e.g. from `.only()` or `.defer()`), setting it onto `rel_obj` meant `rel_obj` was cached with an incomplete parent instance. Moreover:
- If a prefetch had already fetched or populated the relation on `rel_obj` (e.g. via an inner or nested prefetch), assigning `instance` unconditionally overwrote that prefetched instance.
- In multi-level prefetches (e.g. `profile__user`), setting the parent `instance` on `rel_obj` at level 0 caused subsequent levels to consider the relation already fetched, skipping the prefetch.

### Solution
In [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py):
- Check that the parent instance does not have deferred fields (`not instance.get_deferred_fields()`) before caching it on `rel_obj`.
- Check that the relation has not already been cached on `rel_obj` (`not is_cached(rel_obj)`) to avoid overwriting previously prefetched related instances.
